MARKET.head: Bordeaux leads fine wine trade at 39.6% share; Lafite 2005 tops sales
MARKET.summ: Bordeaux led the market, claiming 39.6%, Lafite accounting for over a quarter of its trade
takeaways: Bordeaux claimed 39.6% of traded fine wine value this week, with Lafite accounting for over a quarter of it.
Burgundy fell to 18.4% from 24.8% last week, while Tuscany rose from 5.2% to 8.9%.
The US took a 7.0% share, with US buyers accounting for 58% of their region's purchasing by value.

MARKET.head: VINITECH-SIFEL 2026 trade show set for Bordeaux, December 1-3
MARKET.summ: From 1-3 December 2026, Bordeaux will welcome wine professionals from around the world for VINITECH-SIFEL, a leading international trade show dedicated to innovation and solutions for the wine, fruit and vegetable sectors. Bringing together 700 exhibitors, 40,000 professionals from 70 countries and 70,000 m² of exhibition...
takeaways: VINITECH-SIFEL, a wine, fruit and vegetable trade show, runs 1-3 December 2026 in Bordeaux with 700 exhibitors.
The event expects 40,000 professionals from 70 countries across 70,000 m² of exhibition space.
An International Buyers Program offers eligible international buyers 4-star hotel stays and travel cost support.

MARKET.head: Vinitaly.USA debuts in New York City at Pier 36 in October 2026
MARKET.summ: The Italian wine trade event makes its New York City debut October 26 and 27, bringing 300 exhibitors and 2,500 wines to Pier 36
takeaways: Vinitaly.USA, organized by Veronafiere with the Italian Trade Agency, holds its first New York City edition at Pier 36 on October 26-27, 2026.
The fair moves from Chicago after two years and will host 300 exhibitors presenting 2,500 Italian wine labels, its largest count yet.
Alongside it, the wine2wine Vinitaly Business Forum and Vinitaly International Academy return, with registration now open online.

MARKET.head: Global wine demand shifts from red toward white and sparkling styles
MARKET.summ: The global wine industry has been undergoing a significant structural transformation. While declining overall wine consumption has attracted considerable attention, another important trend has emerged beneath the surface: a steady shift in consumer demand from red wine towards white and sparkling wine.
takeaways: IWSR data shows red wine's share of global consumption fell from about 52 per cent in 2012 to 43 per cent in 2025.
Over the same period, white wine rose from 31 to 34 per cent and sparkling from 8 to 13 per cent.
The shift is reshaping vineyard investment, production strategy and export opportunities, a challenge for Australia's red-led reputation.

MARKET.head: Seven proposed US AVAs spanning California, Oregon, New Jersey and New York await TTB approval
MARKET.summ: From Minnesota to New Jersey, seven proposed AVAs aim to distinguish emerging regions by climate, soils, and grape varieties
takeaways: Seven proposed American Viticultural Areas, from California to Minnesota and New Jersey, await Alcohol and Tobacco Tax and Trade Bureau approval, which can take years.
The proposed Deschutes River AVA would be central Oregon's first recognized winegrowing region, covering 723,760 acres between the Cascade Range and Ochoco Mountains.
The proposed Lake Hennessey AVA would add 4,495 acres to the Napa Valley AVA, with about 355 acres planted mostly to Cabernet Sauvignon.

MARKET.head: VinePair's weekly roundup covers spirits sale talks, drinks industry news and new releases
MARKET.summ: This is VinePair’s Booze News Weekly Roundup, where we gather the hottest headlines and product releases every Friday for a snapshot of what’s happening in the beverage alcohol industry. This week, we have updates on Uncle Nearest’s potential buyers, Mark Zuckerberg’s Guinness flop, the latest product releases, and more.
takeaways: Uncle Nearest, the Tennessee whiskey brand, is reportedly attracting potential buyers.
Southern Glazer's faces a bribery issue, and OpenTable published its 2026 restaurant report.
Pop-Tarts is exiting its BuzzBallz collaboration, and Trump has banned Canadian alcohol.

CULTURE.head: Eight Bordeaux producers showcased as guides to the region's modern wines
CULTURE.summ: Bordeaux put the idea of fine wine on the map. The 1855 Classification became a model for identifying quality wines and producers, a concept copied throughout the region, as well as the world over. But anyone who’s been to Bordeaux knows that those Classified Growths don’t reflect how dynamic and forward-thinking Bordeaux is today.
takeaways: Wine writers compiled a list of eight Bordeaux producers to help newcomers explore the region's modern landscape beyond the 1855 Classification.
The list spans historic châteaux such as Haut-Brion and Château d'Yquem to experimental estates like Durfort-Vivens, which ages wine in amphora.
Entry-point labels highlighted include Clarendelle from Haut-Brion's owner at about $23, and Angelus's third wine No. 3 d'Angelus at about $60.

CULTURE.head: Kathleen Burk's new 600-page global history traces wine from Georgia onward
CULTURE.summ: Kathleen Burk, Wine: A Global History (Basic Books, 2026). Kathleen Burk has written a big book (almost 600 pages) on an even bigger topic, the global history of wine. It is an impressive achievement that will please casual readers and reward detailed study.
takeaways: Historian Kathleen Burk's 'Wine: A Global History' (Basic Books, 2026) runs almost 600 pages, beginning with Georgia's wine cradle.
The book has chapters on Greece, Rome, Venetian, Genoese and Dutch trade, Islam and wine, France, the US, China, and Japan, Korea and Singapore.
The reviewer found the China and Islam chapters most interesting and says the contemporary-world chapter disappointed him.

CULTURE.head: Yinchuan hosts first Asian OIV World Congress with 600 delegates from 47 countries
CULTURE.summ: China hosted the 47th OIV World Congress of Vine and Wine, marking a historic first for Asia
takeaways: China hosted the 47th OIV World Congress of Vine and Wine in Yinchuan, Ningxia, from 12 to 16 October 2026.
It is the first OIV World Congress held in Asia, drawing more than 600 participants from 47 countries.
The congress featured 420 scientific contributions and six technical visits, with presentations to appear open-access on the IVES platform.

CULTURE.head: Cloudy and unfiltered wines gain ground in British supermarkets and restaurants
CULTURE.summ:
There’s something refreshing about unfiltered or unfined wines. We filter through a selection …

Centuries ago, Geoffrey Chaucer observed that “ther is no newe gyse that it nas old”. This truth - that there is nothing new under the sun - certainly applies to wine: every year, a well-documented or ancient viticultural...
takeaways: M&S sells Trouble, a cloudy organic rosé, described as the first cloudy still wine in a British supermarket.
Pét nat is bottled before fermentation finishes and usually not disgorged, which leaves it cloudy.
Zainab Majerikova, head of wine for the Ottolenghi group, says cloudy wines add texture and suit food with complex flavours.

CULTURE.head: Bartenders say American drinkers abroad are curious, though vodka and custom orders persist
CULTURE.summ: Over decades of regular trips to Europe, Regine Rousseau, the Chicago-based founder of wine marketing and events consultancy Shall We Wine, never really subscribed to the directive often preached by U.S. travel publications: When traveling abroad, try not to let your American show. “Number one: I like wearing really bright...
takeaways: European bartenders at London's Connaught Bar and Madrid's Rosewood Villa Magna say American visitors are curious and openly engaged.
Americans still favour vodka Martinis, customised classics and spirit swaps, which bartenders say they are used to fielding.
US visits to Europe hit a record 24 million trips in 2025, with another 5 percent rise expected this year.

SCIENCE.head: NOAA Warns El Niño Could Be Strongest Since 1950, Affecting Wine Regions Worldwide
SCIENCE.summ: This year’s “super El Niño” could be the strongest since 1950. Here’s what that means for winemakers around the world, from welcome rainfall to devastating storms
takeaways: NOAA issued an El Niño advisory on June 11, with an 83 percent chance of surface temperatures up to 2.5 degrees Celsius above average late in 2026.
El Niño can bring more rain, humidity and delayed harvests to regions such as Chile and Santa Barbara, while Australia and South Africa face drought or heat risks.
Winemakers in Chile and Santa Barbara expect rain-related challenges, including cloud cover that can delay harvest by up to two weeks.

SCIENCE.head: Brazilian tropical semi-arid red wines keep polyphenols above literature levels after a year
SCIENCE.summ: Young varietal and experimental wines from Vitis vinifera - Petit Verdot, Tempranillo, and Syrah - cultivated in a tropical semiarid region (Northeast Brazil) were evaluated with regard to their phenolic composition and chromatic characteristics during a storage period of 12-month
takeaways: Researchers from Brazilian universities and Embrapa tracked young Petit Verdot, Tempranillo and Syrah wines from the São Francisco Valley over 12 months of bottle storage.
Petit Verdot showed less colour variation than wines from temperate climates, and polyphenol levels stayed above published figures.
A separate sensory study found red wines grew softer in flavour over storage while whites stayed refreshing, though all wines lost some sensory character.

SCIENCE.head: Tropical wine production grows in Brazil, India, Thailand and Venezuela
SCIENCE.summ: A lot of grapes are produced in the tropics, but only a little part is used to winemaking, what represents some million liters of tropical wines produced per year. The present industry of tropical wine production began 30 years ago
takeaways: Tropical wine production began about 30 years ago and now has commercial wineries in Brazil, India, Thailand and Venezuela.
The authors predict high-quality tropical wines in expressive volumes are achievable in the near future, despite marketing challenges.

SCIENCE.head: Undervine heat tents reveal cultivar-dependent effects on grapevine fruit set
SCIENCE.summ: In the 2009/2010 growing season undervine tents (a passive, open system) were used to increase daytime temperature by 3-5 oC over ambient during the growing season. Four grapevine cultivars (Cabernet Franc, Chardonnay, Semillon and Shiraz) were assessed for reproductive performance under these conditions
takeaways: In 2009/2010, researchers used undervine tents to raise daytime temperatures 3-5 degrees Celsius over ambient in four cultivars.
Chardonnay under heat had lower fruit set, fewer berries and lighter bunches, with reduced pollen tube growth.
Semillon and Shiraz under heat set more fruit and grew more pollen tubes into the ovary; Cabernet Franc showed no significant change.

SCIENCE.head: Part Two of vineyard lab series examines how irrigation water affects soil minerals
SCIENCE.summ: THURSDAY, OCTOBER 8, 2026. BY STAN GRANT, VITICULTURIST. Part Two of a Three-Part Vineyard Mineral Nutrient Management Lab Analysis Series.
takeaways: Viticulturist Stan Grant's second article in a three-part series on lab analysis for vineyard mineral nutrient management addresses irrigation water.
Nearly pure irrigation water, such as Sierra Nevada snowmelt, strips minerals from soil and makes it more acidic over repeated applications.
Alkaline well water high in bicarbonate can form carbonate compounds that reduce its calcium and magnesium fertilizer value.

SCIENCE.head: Cover crops and mulching boost vineyard soil microbes and climate resilience
SCIENCE.summ: Our September newsletter is out. This month: Tasting Climate Change 2026 sessions now available to watch; practical guides on cover crops, weed management and compost teas; fresh research on resilience and economics in regenerative vineyards from France to Sonoma, plus new recognition for ROC and regenerative producers from...
takeaways: A 2026 Environmental Microbiome study in a non-irrigated northern Italian vineyard found cover-crop under-vine mulching raised microbial diversity.
The same study reported improved soil conditions and reduced pathogen pressure under the mulching system.
A 2026 Field Crops Research study of Mediterranean rainfed vineyards found roller-crimped cover crops improved soil cover and vine water status.

SCIENCE.head: French wine harvest set to fall 14% below average after summer heat
SCIENCE.summ:
This year’s harvest expected to be down 2% on mediocre yield in 2025, when production was lowest in nearly 70 years

France’s wine industry is facing a historic low harvest after the country was hit by a series of summer heatwaves.

At about 35m hectolitres, the total harvest would be down 2% on a mediocre 2025...
takeaways: France's 2026 harvest is estimated at about 35 million hectolitres, down 2% on 2025 and 14% below the 2021-2025 average.
Champagne harvested early for the first time in September, with output halved from last year and the five-year average.
Burgundy and Beaujolais projected at 30% below their five-year average, while Bordeaux is expected to rise 10% on 2025.

SCIENCE.head: SFI 2026 offers UK vineyards payments for cover crops and habitat actions
SCIENCE.summ: The second application window for the Sustainable Farming Incentive (SFI) is set to open on 22 September, so Hutchinsons head of environmental services, Georgina Wallis, highlights some actions that may be of interest to growers in the viticulture sector. While the SFI is primarily aimed at arable and livestock farms, vines and...
takeaways: Vineyards and other permanent horticultural crops are within the scope of the Sustainable Farming Incentive (SFI) 2026, alongside arable and livestock farms.
Cover crops for overwinter soil protection must ideally be sown by late August or early September, with SFI allowing up to 12 months to establish a mix.
The RPA is increasingly using satellite imagery to monitor SFI action delivery, and small-seeded cover mixes need a well-prepared, weed-free seedbed.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Profetas e dos Villões: António Maçanita and his remarkable wines from Porto Santo and Madeira
NEWSLETTERS.summ: António Maçanita is a well known Portuguese winemaker, doing good things in the Alentejo, Douro and the Açores
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jamie Goode
takeaways: António Maçanita's Profetas e dos Villões project, with friend Nuno Faria, produces wines from Porto Santo and Madeira.
The project's first wines were made in Madeira; since 2022 a winery operates on Porto Santo, whose arid, flat terrain gets 380 mm of rain yearly.
Wines reviewed include Caracol dos Profetas 2021 and Crosta Calcária 2023, both scored 95 or higher.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Why Michelin Ratings Still Won’t Tell You Who Actually Made Your Burgundy Wine
NEWSLETTERS.summ: This wine guide explains why no critic's score, not even from a renowned guide like Michelin, truly reveals who made your regional wine. Consumer insight is key
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jonathan Finch
takeaways: Since July, some Burgundy bottles carry Michelin ratings of one to three grapes, based on five criteria: agronomy, technical mastery, identity, balance, and consistency.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Wine News: What I’m Reading the Week of 10/18/26
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Hello and welcome to my weekly roundup of the wine stories that I find of interest on the web. I
NEWSLETTERS.author: Alder Yarrow

NEWSLETTERS.head: Pairing Wine With Fall
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Wines to pour with autumnal fare, plus this week’s favorite stories about food, wine, and culture
NEWSLETTERS.author: Meg Maker
takeaways: Meg Maker's Maker's Table piece on fall food and wine pairing opens with a story about lighting the season's first fire at home.
The author argues autumn cuisine in northern New England is earthy, rich, spiced and hearty, with flavors darker than summer's brights.
Maker says pairing is far from a science and is deeply personal and culturally constructed, and promises a list of wine styles for autumn meals.

NEWSLETTERS.head: A Level Playing Field
NEWSLETTERS.summ: What do we mean by the word “Burgundian”? Used indiscriminately to describe a region that is famously, almost defiantly complex, it’s a term that covers so many appellations, terroirs and styles as to be almost meaningless, especially when it comes to white Burgundy. Are we talking Chablis, the Côte Beaune or the Mâconnais?
NEWSLETTERS.author: Tim Atkin MW
takeaways: A blind tasting of 24 wines, 14 from Burgundy (2023s) and 10 from New Zealand (2024s), was organised by Steve Smith MW.
Tim Atkin's top pick was the 2024 Smith & Sheth Onewa Chardonnay from Gimblett Gravels, Hawkes Bay, which he expects to retail for around £60.
Atkin says top Chardonnay is now a level playing field, citing Domaine Leflaive finishing picking on August 18th this year.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Cabernet Franc in the Press: October 2026
NEWSLETTERS.summ: From Livermore to the Loire: Cabernet Franc in Food & Wine, Robb Report, Le Point, JancisRobinson.com, and more
NEWSLETTERS.author: Cab Franc Chronicles
takeaways: Food & Wine reports California had only 3,501 acres of Cabernet Franc in 2025, versus 90,040 acres of Cabernet Sauvignon, per the California Grape Acreage Report.
The Livermore Valley officially named Cabernet Franc and Sauvignon Blanc its signature red and white varieties in February 2025.
JancisRobinson.com profiled Lang & Reed in Napa, founded by John and Tracey Skupny in 1996 solely to make Cabernet Franc.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Telling a mountain to move
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Delving into the details of change in the DO Montsant wine region of Catalunya
NEWSLETTERS.author: Miquel Hudin
takeaways: DO Montsant, in Catalunya, Spain, has revised its bylaws to add certification for 'vi brisat' (orange-style) wines, following DO Terra Alta's similar move in 2022.
Montsant's revised bylaws also create a classification for 'minimal intervention' wines, requiring hand-harvesting, organic certification, spontaneous fermentation and gentle filtration only.
Author Miquel Hudin says the DO did not respond to his request for the maximum sulfur dioxide limit, which is absent from the final published bylaws.

NEWSLETTERS.head: “Unquestionably Among the Greatest Wines in the World” (Tasting the 2024 Port Vintage)
NEWSLETTERS.summ: You’ll find no shortage of Vintage Port coverage on these virtual pages (something that, as I taste more and more vintages of the stuff, has become a source of amusing vexation as I search for whether or not a VP that I want to feature here has already been reviewed and featured here…). And you’ll […] This article was...
NEWSLETTERS.author: Joe Roberts
takeaways: 1WineDude is tasting the 2024 Port vintage and writes that Vintage Port coverage on the site is extensive.
The author notes growing difficulty checking whether a given Vintage Port has already been reviewed on the site.

NEWSLETTERS.head: 400 Montepulciano Bottles for Thomas Jefferson circa 1805
NEWSLETTERS.summ: The wine everyone’s been gushing over since the middle ages!
NEWSLETTERS.author: Eveline Chartier
takeaways: An October 17, 1350 trade contract between the Del Pecora family and merchant Jacopo di Vanni is the oldest known document for Vino Nobile di Montepulciano, held in Florence's State Archives.
A 2024 document from the Consorzio del Vino Nobile di Montepulciano dates the first known use of the term 'Vino Nobile' to 1766 by the Jesuits, not 1787.
In April 1806 Thomas Jefferson asked Thomas Appleton for 400 bottles of Montepulciano annually after receiving 473 bottles in November 1805.

NEWSLETTERS.head: The Encyclopedia of Wine - Fresh Take or Same Same?
NEWSLETTERS.summ: I take a look at a brand new reference work to see how it stacks up with the competition
NEWSLETTERS.author: Simon J. Woolf
takeaways: Dorling Kindersley's The Encyclopedia of Wine publishes 8 October in the UK and 10 November in the US.
Editor-in-chief David Williams aims for an authoritative but accessible reference, written by 28 contributing experts including Jane Anson and Wink Lorch.
The 400-page book is positioned against Oxford Companion to Wine and The World Atlas of Wine, both produced by Jancis Robinson's team.
